IEA Wind Resource Assessment - Data Model

Type: object

This Data Model schema is a digital representation of a meteorological mast used for measuring the wind resource of a potential wind farm.

root author

Author

Type: string

The person or system who created this data model representing a specific mast.
Examples:

"Stephen Holleran"

"Joe Bloggs"

root organisation

Organisation

Type: string

The organisation the Author is from.
Examples:

"brightwind"

"Wind Developer Ltd."

root date

Date

Type: stringFormat: date

The date this file was created. Format should be YYYY-MM-DD
Example:

"2020-07-28"

root version

Version

Type: string

The version of the IEA WRA Data Model this file is based on. The format of this follows Semantic Versioning with the year and month tagged on after. E.g. 1.1.1-2020.07

Must match regular expression: ^([0-9]{1,2})[.]([0-9]{1,2})[.]([0-9]{1,2})-([0-9]{4})[.]([0-9]{2})$
Examples:

"0.1.0-2020.06"

"1.1.1-2020.07"

root license

License

Type: string or null

Expected to be used as the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative intended. Link: http://purl.org/dc/terms/license Definition: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Comment: Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
Examples:

"https://opensource.org/license/bsd-3-clause/"

"BSD-3-Clause"

root plant_name

Plant Name

Type: string or null

The name of the wind farm this met mast is associated with.
Example:

"A Name of Wind Farm"

root plant_type

Plant Type

Type: enum (of null or string)

The type of renewable generation plant it is.

Must be one of:

  • "onshore_wind"
  • "offshore_wind"
  • "solar"
  • null

root measurement_location

Measurement Location

Type: array of object

This is the geographic location of the meteorological measurement station i.e. a met mast/tower or remote sensing device.

All items must be unique

No Additional Items

Each item of this array must be:

Measurement Location


No Additional Properties

root measurement_location Measurement Location uuid

UUID

Type: string or nullFormat: uuid

The unique identifier of the measurement location in the UUID format. A UUID can be generated here https://www.uuidgenerator.net/
Example:

"3d40f012-a525-4024-a626-5fcf954c59cf"

root measurement_location Measurement Location name

Name

Type: string

The name given to the measurement location i.e. to the met mast or remote sensing device. Unique names are recommended to avoid two locations in the same context being given the same name.
Example:

"AName_MM1"

root measurement_location Measurement Location latitude_ddeg

Latitude [ddeg]

Type: number

Latitude coordinate in the Geographic Coordinate System using the WGS84 reference coordinate system, EPSG:4326. Unit of measure is in decimal degrees. Latitude lines are parallel to the equator where their position ranges from -90 degrees at the south pole to 90 degrees at the north pole.

Value must be greater or equal to -90 and lesser or equal to 90


Example:

52.973

root measurement_location Measurement Location longitude_ddeg

Longitude [ddeg]

Type: number

Longitude coordinate in the Geographic Coordinate System using the WGS84 reference coordinate system, EPSG:4326. Unit of measure is in decimal degrees. Longitude lines are perpendicular to the equator where their position ranges from 0° at Greenwich Mean Time increasing to +180° as you move eastward and decreasing to −180° as you move westward.

Value must be greater or equal to -180 and lesser or equal to 180


Example:

-9.431

root measurement_location Measurement Location measurement_station_type_id

Measurement Station Type

Type: enum (of string)

The type of measurement station. This must be one of either met mast, lidar (a vertical profiler), sodar (also a vertical profiler), floating lidar (floating vertical profiler lidar), wave buoy, ADCP (Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler) or a solar measurement station.

Must be one of:

  • "mast"
  • "lidar"
  • "sodar"
  • "floating_lidar"
  • "wave_buoy"
  • "seabed_frame"
  • "moored"
  • "adcp"
  • "solar"
  • "virtual_met_mast"
  • "reanalysis"

root measurement_location Measurement Location notes

Notes

Type: string or null

Notes relating to these properties.
Example:

"I can write anything I want here."

root measurement_location Measurement Location update_at

Date of Update

Type: string or null

The date these properties were last updated.
Example:

"2020-07-28T20:49:13"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties

Mast Properties

Type: object or null

The properties of the installed met mast/tower. Additional properties can be added e.g. 'material' however this wouldn't be part of the Data Model. If an additional property is for information purposes please consider using 'notes' instead.

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_geometry_id

Mast Geometry

Type: enum (of null or string)

The type of mast geometry e.g. lattice with a triangular profile or pole. The IEC specifies two square lattice towers as having rounded edges for their members or sharp edges.

Must be one of:

  • "lattice_triangle"
  • "lattice_square_round_edges"
  • "lattice_square_sharp_edges"
  • "pole"
  • null

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_oem

Mast OEM

Type: string or null

The manufacturer of the met mast.
Examples:

"NRG Systems"

"Galetech Energy Services"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_serial_number

Mast Serial Number

Type: string or null

The manufacturer's serial number of the mast.
Examples:

"XHD12345"

"MM01234"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_model

Mast Model

Type: string or null

The model of the mast.
Examples:

"80m XHD TallTower"

"SLX80m"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_height_m

Mast Height [m]

Type: number or null

The height of the mast itself, not necessarily the top anemometer height.
Example:

81.3

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties date_from

Date From

Type: string or nullFormat: date-time

The date from when these properties are active. If these properties follow a change, then this Date From should equal the previous Date To. The format of this date should follow ISO 8601 with the 'T' required. If a timezone is used, it is essential that this timezone is the same as the logger timezone.
Example:

"2020-07-28T20:00:00"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties date_to

Date To

Type: string or null

The final end date for when these properties are active. If these properties are currently active please use null. If null is not allowed please use 2100-01-01T00:00:00. The format of this date should follow ISO 8601 with the 'T' required. If a timezone is used, it is essential that this timezone is the same as the logger timezone.
Examples:

"2020-07-28T20:00:00"

"2100-01-01T00:00:00"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties notes

Notes

Type: string or null

Notes relating to these properties.

Same definition as notes

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties update_at

Date of Update

Type: string or null

The date these properties were last updated.

Same definition as update_at

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry

Mast Section Geometry

Type: array of object or null

This contains the properties of each mast section. Additional properties can be added e.g. 'material' however this wouldn't be part of the Data Model. If an additional property is for information purposes please consider using 'notes' instead.

All items must be unique

No Additional Items

Each item of this array must be:

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry

Mast Section Geometry

Type: object

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry uuid

UUID

Type: string or nullFormat: uuid

The unique id to relate this mast section to the mounting arrangement. A UUID can be generated here https://www.uuidgenerator.net/
Example:

"bf078172-bbb6-48fe-ac1f-c6605dffb1b5"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry mast_section_height_mm

Mast Section Height [mm]

Type: number or null

Towers come in sections that are connected together to make a complete met mast. This is the height in mm of this met mast section.
Example:

6000

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry pole_diameter_mm

Pole Diameter [mm]

Type: number or null

If a pole mast is used, it's diameter in mm.
Example:

203

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_face_width_at_bottom_mm

Lattice Face Width at Bottom [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice face width at the bottom of the mast section, as measured from leg centre to leg centre as outlined in IEC 61400-12-1 2017 Fig G.5.
Example:

500

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_face_width_at_top_mm

Lattice Face Width at Top [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice face width at the top of the mast section, as measured from leg centre to leg centre as outlined in IEC 61400-12-1 2017 Fig G.5.
Example:

500

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_leg_width_mm

Lattice Leg Width [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice leg diameter for a round leg or width for a square cross section leg.
Example:

50

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_leg_is_round_cross_section

Lattice Leg is Round Cross Section

Type: boolean or null

The lattice leg is a round or square cross section. True is for a round leg cross section and false is for a square leg cross section.
Examples:

"true (for a round leg cross section)"

"false (for a square leg cross section)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_bracing_member_diameter_mm

Lattice Bracing Member Diameter [mm]

Type: number or null

THIS FIELD WILL BE DEPRECIATED IN THE NEXT MAJOR RELEASE. The lattice diagonal bracing member diameter.
Example:

12

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_bracing_member_diameter_horizontal_mm

Lattice Bracing Member Diameter Horizontal [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice horizontal bracing member diameter in mm.
Example:

12

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_bracing_member_diameter_diagonal_mm

Lattice Bracing Member Diameter Diagonal [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice diagonal bracing member diameter in mm.
Example:

12

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_number_of_diagonal_bracing_members

Lattice Number of Bracing Members

Type: integer or null

The number of lattice diagonal bracing members that are contained in one of the repetitive patterns making up a mast section.
Examples:

1

2

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_bracing_member_length_diagonal_mm

Lattice Bracing Member Length Diagonal [mm]

Type: number or null

The lattice diagonal bracing member length in mm.
Example:

512

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry number_of_repetitive_patterns_on_face

Number of Repetitive Patterns on Face

Type: integer or null

The number of repetitive patterns on tower face as in the image. Note that for this case the pattern in red repeats itself 6 times. https://github.com/IEA-Task-43/digitalwradatastandard/blob/master/images/numberofrepetitivepatternsonface.png.
Example:

6

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_bracing_member_height_mm

Lattice Bracing Member Height [mm]

Type: number or null

The height of the lattice diagonal bracing members.
Example:

900

root measurement_location Measurement Location mast_properties mast_section_geometry Mast Section Geometry lattice_has_horizontal_member

Does the tower have horizontal braces?

Type: boolean or null

This represents masts that have horizontal braces. True is for towers with horizontal braces and false is for towers without horizontal braces.
Examples:

"true (for towers with horizontal braces)"

"false (for towers without horizontal braces)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties

Vertical Profiler Properties

Type: array of object or null

Vertical profiler remote sensing devices (e.g. lidar, sodar and floating lidar) installation specific properties.

All items must be unique

No Additional Items

Each item of this array must be:

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties

Vertical Profiler Properties

Type: object
No Additional Properties

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties device_datum_plane_height_m

Device Datum Plane Height [m]

Type: number or null

The datum plane height of the remote sensing device where the datum feature is defined here: http://data.windenergy.dtu.dk/ontologies/view/ontolidar/en/page/DatumFeature . For lidars the datum feature is usually the window and for sodars it is usually the base of the device. These datum plane heights are also usually referred to as above ground level however it may be above sea level or above a platform level.
Examples:

0.5

1

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties height_reference_id

Height Reference

Type: enum (of null or string) Default: "ground_level"

The height reference frame that is used to measure the item height. E.g. onshore this is 'ground level' i.e. the item is 0.5 m above ground level. Offshore is a bit different as it can be 20 m above 'mean sea level' or 20 m above 'lowest astronomical tide' for a fixed structure or 20 m above 'sea level' for a floating lidar.

Must be one of:

  • "ground_level"
  • "mean_sea_level"
  • "sea_level"
  • "lowest_astronomical_tide"
  • "sea_floor"
  • "other"
  • null

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties device_orientation_deg

Device Orientation [deg]

Type: number or null

The orientation that the remote sensing device is installed relative to north.

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties orientation_reference_id

Orientation Reference

Type: enum (of null or string)

The orientation reference the item is measured against. E.g. magnetic north.

Must be one of:

  • "magnetic_north"
  • "true_north"
  • "grid_north"
  • null

root measurement_location Measurement Location vertical_profiler_properties Vertical Profiler Properties device_vertical_orientation

Device Vertical Orientation

Type: enum (of null or string)

The vertical orientation that the remote sensing device is installed. E.g. an ADCP mounted on the sea floor has an 'upwards' vertical orientation pointing towards the sea surface whereas an ADCP mounted underneath a buoy has a 'downward' vertical orientation pointing towards the sea floor.

Must be one of:

  • "upward"
  • "downward"
  • null

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config

Logger Configuration

Type: array of object

This represents how the logger's main settings are configured. For example, it's sampling rate or averaging period. For remote sensing devices, such as lidar's, the device itself is considered as a logger and so these logger configuration attributes should be used to describe the lidar.

All items must be unique

No Additional Items

Each item of this array must be:

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration

Logger Configuration

Type: object

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_oem_id

Logger OEM


The logger or remote sensing device manufacturer's name. In WRA Data Model versions 1.4.0 and before this was an enum; it now accepts a free-text string for forward compatibility. It is strongly advised to use a value from the suggestion list. If the manufacturer is not listed, use their official name, spelling and casing so it can be added to the list in a future release. For floating lidars where the data is sometimes packaged together onshore, this value could be the floating lidar device OEM.

  • Option 1
  • Option 2

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_model_name

Logger Model Name

Type: string or null

This is the logger or remote sensing device model name. This is usually stated in the data files from the logger in either the header or footer.
Examples:

"Symphonie Plus3"

"CR1000"

"Meteo-40M"

"WindCube v2"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_serial_number

Logger Serial Number

Type: string

The logger or remote sensing device serial number. This is sometimes different from the logger id.

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_firmware_version

Logger Firmware Version

Type: string or null

The logger or remote sensing device's Firmware Version. This is the software version that is run on the logger at the time of data acquisition. This software can be updated and so can sometimes impact the results of the outputted data. E.g. NRG SymphoniePro, Firmware Version: 3.2.3. For loggers/devices that have multiple software programmes to process the outputted data the versions can be concatenated together.

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_id

Logger Id

Type: string or null

This is the logger or remote sensing device id. It may be set by the logger programmer and may be different from the logger serial number.
Examples:

"4321"

"D123456"

"WLS7-999"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_name

Logger Name

Type: string or null

The logger (or mast name) name assigned to the logger in the logger programme.
Example:

"AName_MM1"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration date_from

Date From

Type: string

The date from when these properties are active. If these properties follow a change, then this Date From should equal the previous Date To. The format of this date should follow ISO 8601 with the 'T' required. If a timezone is used, it is essential that this timezone is the same as the logger timezone.
Example:

"2020-07-28T20:00:00"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration date_to

Date To

Type: string or null

The final end date for when these properties are active. If these properties are currently active please use null. If null is not allowed please use 2100-01-01T00:00:00. The format of this date should follow ISO 8601 with the 'T' required. If a timezone is used, it is essential that this timezone is the same as the logger timezone.

Same definition as date_to

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration encryption_pin_or_key

Type: string or null

The encryption PIN or key used to encrypt the data.
Examples:

"9876"

"KkocDuSCk3v5tw4kRveHGQvuD1kYVVbU"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration enclosure_lock_details

Enclosure Lock Details

Type: string or null

Details about how to open the logger enclosure box when on site.

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration data_transfer_details

Data Transfer Details

Type: string or null

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration offset_from_utc_hrs

Offset From UTC [hr]

Type: number or null

The number of hours that the resulting timeseries dataset is offset from UTC. E.g. -5 for Eastern Standard Time.
Examples:

"-5 (for Eastern Standard Time)"

"1 (for Central European Time)"

"5.5 (for India Standard Time)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration sampling_rate_sec

Sampling Rate [s]

Type: integer or null

The number of seconds the logger samples data.
Examples:

"1"

"2"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration averaging_period_minutes

Averaging Period [min]

Type: integer or null

The number of minutes the model outputs the timeseries data at. Also known as 'time step' or 'averaging step'
Examples:

"10"

"60"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration timestamp_is_end_of_period

Timestamp at End of Period

Type: boolean or null

Does the timestamp represent the end of the averaging period. True is for timestamp to represent the end of the averaging period and false is for timestamp to represent the start of the averaging period.
Examples:

"true (for timestamp to represent the end of the averaging period)"

"false (for timestamp to represent the start of the averaging period)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration clock_is_auto_synced

Clock is Auto-Synced

Type: boolean or null

Is the logger clock auto-synced with an internet time server to keep accurate time. True is for when the logger clock is auto-synced and false is for when the logger clock is not auto-synced.
Examples:

"true (for when the logger clock is auto-synced)"

"false (for when the logger clock is not auto-synced)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration logger_acquisition_uncertainty

Logger Acquisition Uncertainty [%]

Type: number or null

The uncertainty of the logger acquisition system as a percentage. This is also referred to as the uncertainty of the data acquisition system within IEC 61400-12-1.


Example:

"0.1"

root measurement_location Measurement Location logger_main_config Logger Configuration uncertainty_k_factor

Uncertainty K Factor

Type: number or null

Uncertainty k factor for Logger Acquisition Uncertainty as provided in logger documentation specification.
Example:

"2"

The final end date for when these properties are active. If these properties are currently active please use null. If null is not allowed please use 2100-01-01T00:00:00. The format of this date should follow ISO 8601 with the 'T' required. If a timezone is used, it is essential that this timezone is the same as the logger timezone.

Same definition as date_to

In WRA Data Model versions 1.4.0 and before this was an enum; it now accepts a free-text string for forward compatibility with newer datasets. It is strongly advised to use a value from the enum list, matching the dataset producer's official name, spelling and casing.

Examples:

"wind_speed  (the horizontal component of wind speed)"

"wind_direction  (the direction from which the wind is coming from)"

"air_temperature  (outdoor ambient temperature of the air)"

"water_temperature  (is the in situ temperature of the water. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_temperature'.)"

"temperature  (the temperature of a body or indoor ambient air temperature)"

"dew_point_temperature  (the temperature to which air must be cooled, at constant barometric pressure and with fixed water vapor content, for the air to become fully saturated with water vapor i.e. 100% relative humidity)"

"air_pressure (outdoor pressure of the air)"

"water_pressure (the pressure of water. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_pressure' and includes the pressure due to overlying sea water, sea ice, air and any other medium that may be present.)"

"pressure (the pressure of a medium.)"

"air_density (the density of air)"

"relative_humidity (outdoor relative humidity of the air"

"voltage (electrical voltage, typically the logger battery voltage)"

"current (electrical current, typically the logger battery current)"

"resistance (electrical resistance, the raw or basic measurement from many different sensors)"

"power (the amount of energy transferred or converted per unit of time)"

"energy (in physics, is the capacity for doing work. It may exist in potential, kinetic, thermal, electrical, chemical, nuclear, or other various forms.)"

"vertical_wind_speed (the vertical component of wind speed)"

"wind_speed_turbulence (the turbulence of the wind speed)"

"precipitation (water which falls to the ground from the atmosphere in forms of rain, snow, sleet, ice pellets, dew, frost, and hail)"

"ice_detection (detection of ice build up on surfaces)"

"global_horizontal_irradiance (the total power or instantaneous rate of energy from the sun received by a horizontal surface on Earth)"

"direct_normal_irradiance (the direct line of sight power or instantaneous rate of energy from the sun, excluding diffuse irradiance, received by a surface on Earth perpendicular to the sun)"

"diffuse_horizontal_irradiance (the power or instantaneous rate of energy from light scattered by the atmosphere, excluding direct irradiance, received by a horizontal surface on Earth)"

"global_tilted_irradiance (the total power or instantaneous rate of energy from the sun received by a surface on Earth with defined tilt and azimuth, fixed or sun-tracking)"

"global_normal_irradiance (the total power or instantaneous rate of energy from the sun received by a surface on Earth perpendicular to the sun)"

"albedo (or reflected solar radiation from the earth's surface, is defined as the ratio between the reflected energy and the incident energy over a unit area)"

"soiling_loss_index (an index of lost energy between clean and dirty PV modules, https://www.campbellsci.com/cr-pvs1 )"

"illuminance (measure of visible light falling onto a per unit area, typically measured in lux)"

"fog (is a visible aerosol consisting of tiny water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the air at or near the Earth's surface)"

"salinity (is the salt content of water. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_salinity', 'sea_water_practical_salinity' or 'sea_water_absolute_salinity' depending on the scale been used.)"

"conductivity (of an electrolyte solution, e.g. sea water, is a measure of its ability to conduct electricity. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_electrical_conductivity' for offshore use cases.)"

"specific_conductivity (of an electrolyte solution, e.g. sea water, is a measure of its ability to conduct electricity at a specific temperature. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_electrical_conductivity_at_reference_temperature'.)"

"density_anomaly (is the density of seawater minus 1000 kg/m³, expressed this way so small but important density differences are easier to work with.)"

"gps_coordinates (latitude and/or longitude as measured by a gps)"

"status (a status flag or other to describe the status of a sensor or object)"

"counter (a simple counter)"

"availability (the availability of a sensor or the presence of something in a measurement typically measured as %, e.g. '40m Data Availability (%)' or 'Proportion Of Packets with Fog (%)'. This is currently a generic catch-all for all 'availability' like metrics and may be resolved into more specific definitions in future revisions.)"

"quality (a measure of the quality of a measurement)"

"carrier_to_noise_ratio (a measure of signal strength as measured by lidar devices, http://data.windenergy.dtu.dk/ontologies/view/IEATask32Glossary/en/page/parameters.carrier_to_noise_ratio )"

"doppler_spectral_broadening (as measured by lidar devices)"

"echo_intensity (is the brightness or brilliance of the acoustic echo usually measured by an ADCP. If from an ADCP, it can be used to judge the quality of measurement or estimate the amount of suspended sediment in the water column.)"

"signal_to_noise_ratio (a measure of signal strength as measured by ADCPs.)"

"motion_corrected_wind_speed (the horizontal component of wind speed which has been corrected due to the motion of the measuring sensor/device, typically from floating lidar systems)"

"motion_corrected_wind_direction (the direction form which the wind is coming from which has been corrected due to the motion of the measuring sensor/device, typically from floating lidar systems)"

"motion_corrected_vertical_wind_speed (the vertical component of wind speed which has been corrected due to the motion of the measuring sensor/device, typically from floating lidar systems)"

"wave_height (is the mean wave height measured during the observation period, where the height is defined as the vertical distance from a wave trough to the following wave crest. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_mean_height'.)"

"wave_significant_height (is a statistic computed from wave measurements and corresponds to the average height of the highest one third of the waves, where the height is defined as the vertical distance from a wave trough to the following wave crest. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_significant_height'.)"

"wave_maximum_height (is the greatest trough to crest distance measured during the observation period. Wave height is defined as the vertical distance from a wave trough to the following wave crest. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_maximum_height'.)"

"wave_direction (the direction from which the wave is coming from. The direction is a bearing in the usual geographical sense, measured positive clockwise from due north. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_from_direction'.)"

"wave_directional_spread (is the standard deviation of all the wave directions measured. It signifies how spread out,or how wide an area, all the waves are coming from. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_directional_spread'.)"

"wave_period (is the mean wave period measured during the observation period at a specific location. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_mean_period'.)"

"wave_peak_period (is the wave period of the most energetic waves in the total wave spectrum at a specific location. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_period_at_variance_spectral_density_maximum'.)"

"wave_period_first_frequency (commonly referred to as Tm01, is the mean wave period calculated from the wave energy spectrum as the ratio of the zeroth spectral moment (m0) and the first spectral moment (m1). It represents the energy-weighted average period of sea surface waves and provides an estimate of the characteristic wave period that carries most of the energy in the sea state. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_mean_period_from_variance_spectral_density_first_frequency_moment'.)"

"wave_period_second_frequency (commonly referred to as Tm02, is the mean wave period calculated from the wave energy spectrum using the ratio of the square root of the zeroth spectral moment (m0) to the second spectral moment (m2). It provides an estimate of the average wave period weighted more heavily toward higher frequencies, making it sensitive to shorter, more energetic waves in the sea state. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_mean_period_from_variance_spectral_density_second_frequency_moment'.)"

"wave_period_zero_crossing (is the average time interval between successive individual waves where the sea surface elevation passes upwards through its mean level. In CF Conventions there is no equivalent standard name, however there is the alias 'sea_surface_wave_zero_upcrossing_period' which is part of the standard 'sea_surface_wave_mean_period'.)"

"wave_energy_spectrum (is a representation of how the energy (or variance) of sea surface waves is distributed across different frequencies, typically expressed in units of m^2/Hz. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_variance_spectral_density'.)"

"wave_energy_spectrum_maximum (also referred to as the peak wave energy, is the highest spectral density value within the wave energy spectrum, indicating the greatest energy concentration at a specific frequency. This frequency is commonly used to define the peak wave period, which characterizes the dominant waves in the sea state. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_surface_wave_energy_at_variance_spectral_density_maximum'.)"

"water_speed (the horizontal magnitude of the water's velocity. This is sometimes also known as 'current speed' and in CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_speed'.)"

"vertical_water_speed (the vertical magnitude of the water's velocity. In CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'upward_sea_water_velocity'.)"

"water_direction (the direction from which the water flow is coming from. The direction is a bearing in the usual geographical sense, measured positive clockwise from due north. This is sometimes also known as 'current direction' and in CF Conventions this is equivalent to 'sea_water_velocity_from_direction' or 'sea_water_from_direction'.)"

"orientation (the direction something points or faces relative to north or other specified positions)"

"compass_direction (the direction as measured by a compass, therefore referenced to magnetic north)"

"true_north_offset (the offset something points or faces relative to true north, e.g. from a solar compass such as a Geovane)"

"tilt_x (the tilt of an object relative to the x-axis)"

"tilt_y (the tilt of an object relative to the y-axis)"

"tilt_z (the tilt of an object relative to the z-axis)"

"pitch ((from CF Conventions for 'platform_pitch') is a rotation about an axis that is perpendicular to both the local vertical axis and the nominal forward motion direction of the sensor. If the sensor is the buoy itself, then the 'forward motion direction' can also be known as the 'first principal axis' or the 'buoy's north'. Pitch is relative to the 'at rest' rotation of the sensor with respect to the axis of rotation. The 'at rest' rotation of the sensor may change over time.)"

"roll ((from CF Conventions for 'platform_roll') is a rotation about an axis that is perpendicular to the local vertical axis and is coplanar with the nominal forward motion direction of the sensor. If the sensor is the buoy itself, then the 'forward motion direction' can also be known as the 'first principal axis' or the 'buoy's north'. Roll is relative to the 'at rest' rotation of the sensor with respect to the axis of rotation. The 'at rest' rotation of the sensor may change over time.)"

"heading (also known as yaw, (from CF Conventions for 'platform_yaw') is a rotation about the local vertical axis. Heading is relative to the 'at rest' rotation of the sensor with respect to the axis of rotation. The 'at rest' rotation of the sensor may change over time. In navigation terms, the heading of a vessel or aircraft is the compass direction in which the craft's bow or nose is pointed. Heading is typically based on cardinal directions, so 0° (or 360°) indicates a direction toward true north.)"

"u (the U component vector, relating to wind it is positive for a west to east flow (eastward wind), however, it can be used for other vectors. If so, please use the notes property to define it.)"

"v (the V component vector, relating to wind it is positive for a south to north flow (northward wind), however, it can be used for other vectors. If so, please use the notes property to define it.)"

"w (the W component vector, if using this for wind please use the 'vertical_wind_speed' measurement type. Please use the notes property to define how this component is utilised.)"

"elevation (the height the surface of the earth is above mean sea level)"

"altitude (the height above mean sea level or is the angle between the sun and the observer's local horizon, also sometimes referred to as elevation.)"

"height (the vertical distance above a particular reference e.g. ground level.)"

"azimuth (is the angle of the sun around the horizon, in the northern hemisphere this is usually measured from north and increasing eastward whereas in the southern hemisphere it can be measured from the south and increasing westward.)"

"water_level (is the height of the sea surface above the sea floor. In CF Conventions this is equivalent, but opposite in respect of their point of reference, to 'sea_floor_depth_below_sea_surface'.)"

"depth (the vertical distance below a particular reference e.g. sea level.)"

"fuel_level (is the amount of fuel remaining in a tank or reservoir, typically measured as a percentage or in units like liters.)"

"turbidity (from CF Conventions for 'sea_water_turbidity' the turbidity is a dimensionless quantity which is expressed in NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units), FNU (Formazin Nephelometric Units) or FTU (Formazin Turbidity Units). Turbidity expressed in NTU is the proportion of white light scattered back to a transceiver by the particulate load in a body of water, represented on an arbitrary scale referenced against measurements made in the laboratory on aqueous suspensions of formazine beads.)"

"visibility_in_air ((from CF Conventions for 'visibility_in_air') the visibility is the distance at which something can be seen with Canonical Units of 'm'.)"

"speed_of_sound_in_air (the velocity at which acoustic waves move through the atmosphere.)"

"speed_of_sound_in_water (the velocity at which acoustic waves move through water, such as sea water. In CF Conventions this is known as 'speed_of_sound_in_sea_water'.)"

"mass_concentration (refers to the amount of mass of a substance (X) contained in a given volume of another substance (Y). It is expressed as mass per unit volume. In CF Conventions it typically appears in terms like mass_concentration_of_X_in_Y, where X is the material present in Y.)"

"leaf_surface_wetness (the presence and amount of moisture, such as dew, rain or fog, on the surface of a leaf or a leaf-like sensing element used as a proxy for vegetation wetness.)"

"timestamp (the timestamp of when a measurement value was recorded)"

"obukhov_length (a parameter with a dimension of length which, when used to scale the height above ground, gives a dimensionless stability parameter.)"

"row_checksum (a hash of all other fields in the row used for data integrity verification, e.g. computed using SHA-256)"

"other"

Height Reference

Type: enum (of null or string) Default: "ground_level"

The height reference frame that is used to measure the item height. E.g. onshore this is 'ground level' i.e. the item is 0.5 m above ground level. Offshore is a bit different as it can be 20 m above 'mean sea level' or 20 m above 'lowest astronomical tide' for a fixed structure or 20 m above 'sea level' for a floating lidar.

root measurement_location Measurement Location measurement_point Measurement Point sensor Sensor classification

Classification

Type: string or null

The classification of a particular anemometer for this location. This combines the class index (number) with the terrain class (A, B, C, D or S) e.g. 1.2A. The format of this is validated by a regex which has the form of ^[0-9][.][0-9][ABCDS]$ i.e. digit.digit followed by a character.

Must match regular expression: ^([0-9]{1,2})[.]([0-9]{1,2})[ABCDS]$
Examples:

"1.0A"

"3.2B"

"2.7S"

"10.32S"

root measurement_location Measurement Location measurement_point Measurement Point sensor Sensor instrument_poi_height_mm

Instrument Point of Interest Height [mm]

Type: number or null

This is the physical height dimension, in mm, of the sensor's point of interest, i.e. point of measurement. This is to aid IEC mounting calculations. It is not the height above ground level at which it is deployed. For example, if the sensor is an anemometer it is the height from the bottom of the instrument to the centre of the cups. For a sonic anemometer it is the centre of the sampling volume. For a horizontal propeller anemometer it is the axis of rotation of the propellers. For a wind vane it is the top of the vane.
Example:

"169 mm for a Vector A100 anemometer (https://www.windspeed.co.uk/ws/index.php?option=displaypage&op=page&Itemid=48#dimensions)."

root measurement_location Measurement Location measurement_point Measurement Point sensor Sensor is_heated

Is Heated

Type: boolean or null

Is the sensor heated to reduce the effect of icing. This is usually relevant for wind speed and wind vane sensors. True is for when the sensor is heated and false is for when the sensor is not heated.
Examples:

"true (if the sensor is heated)"

"false (if the sensor is not heated)"

root measurement_location Measurement Location measurement_point Measurement Point sensor Sensor sensor_body_size_mm

Sensor Body Size [mm]

Type: number or null

This is the instrument body size in mm. This parameter is used in IEC 61400-12-2 to ensure that the size of the anemometer body is smaller than the diameter of the tube used to mount the anemometer.
Example:

"50"
